**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 14.2).**

- **Compliant elements:** Section 14.1 confirms we own Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing IP with only a limited processing right to Vendor; Section 14.4 blocks joint ownership and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback; Section 14.3 appropriately limits Vendor to Vendor Technology.
- **The problem:** Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for us, with only a *revocable, non-transferable, term-limited* licence back. That fails the preferred position and also the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables.
- **Why Section 13.2 doesn't cure it:** that perpetual licence covers software and Vendor Technology delivered paid-up or embedded in a Deliverable — not the Deliverable itself — as Section 14.3 confirms.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** flips ownership to Customer with an express irrevocable assignment on creation, while expressly leaving Vendor Technology with Vendor under Sections 14.3 and 13.2. The comment offers the licence-back fallback if Vendor resists assignment.
